metaDescription: Own minerals near Sleepy Hollow outside Gillette, in the Powder River Basin's CBM and oil trend? We check what's actually paying before quoting you.
heroLead: Sleepy Hollow sits just outside Gillette in Campbell County, ground that has seen both the coalbed methane boom of the 2000s and the more recent Niobrara oil drilling that followed it.
intro: Campbell County is the county most people think of when they hear Powder River Basin, and it has been through more than one cycle. Coalbed methane development boomed here in the early 2000s and then largely went bust as gas prices fell and wells were plugged or shut in. More recently, operators have targeted deeper Niobrara and other oil-bearing formations with horizontal wells, a completely different play stacked under some of the same old CBM acreage.

sections.heading: Two different eras, two different interests
paragraphs: If your family's mineral interest near Sleepy Hollow traces to a CBM lease from the coalbed methane era, it is worth checking whether that lease is even still active — many were released after wells were plugged. Separately, deeper horizontal oil development in the county may or may not involve the same tract. We check both possibilities before making an offer, since they are priced very differently.

sections.heading: CBM legacy leases and shut-in wells
paragraphs: A lot of Campbell County CBM leases from the boom years have gone quiet as wells were shut in or plugged, which means the mineral rights may now be unleased and open again. That is not necessarily bad news for a seller — unleased minerals near an active deeper play can carry real value tied to future development rather than a dead CBM well.

sections.heading: What we check first
paragraphs: We pull current Wyoming Oil and Gas Conservation Commission records for your legal description to see whether there is active CBM production, active oil production, or neither, before we put a number together.

faqs.question: My old CBM lease hasn't paid anything in years. Is it dead?
faqs.answer: Possibly — many coalbed methane wells in Campbell County were plugged after the boom ended. We check current status before assuming either way.

faqs.question: If my minerals are unleased, are they worth less?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Unleased minerals near active deeper drilling can be attractive precisely because there's no existing lease terms limiting a new deal.

faqs.question: Is there current oil drilling activity near Sleepy Hollow?
faqs.answer: Campbell County has seen renewed horizontal drilling targeting deeper formations. We check current activity for your specific tract before pricing.

faqs.question: How do I know if my interest is CBM, deeper oil, or both?
faqs.answer: Your division order or lease will usually specify the formation. If it's unclear, we can check Wyoming Oil and Gas Conservation Commission well records to sort it out.
